narrative:
The model determined that you have a 68% chance of representing a bad credit risk. This probability is high enough that the bank decided to deny your loan application.

Your application was turned down primarily because of three key aspects of your financial profile. The most influential factor was your credit history, followed by the status of your checking account, and then the purpose of the loan.

Your credit history of having all paid at this bank is quite rare—only 2.9% of approved applicants share this exact record. Unfortunately, in this dataset the model sees this specific history as a strong signal that pushes your risk upward rather than indicating reliability. The status of your checking account, showing between 0 and 200 DM, also worked against you. While this is not uncommon (18.4% of approved customers have similar balances), the model interpreted it as increasing your likelihood of repayment problems. Finally, requesting the loan for a new car added further upward pressure on the risk score. Although 16.5% of approved applicants borrow for cars, this purpose was viewed less favorably than more common reasons such as radio or furniture.

Taken together, these three factors outweighed the positive signals from your lower-than-average loan amount, shorter duration, and stable employment.

You should focus on improving your credit history by maintaining perfect payments on all existing obligations for the next 12–24 months, and consider building a larger checking-account balance. Once these areas strengthen, reapply or explore smaller loans that better match common successful profiles.
